_description: A USB data-line protector on a 30 x 15 mm two-layer board: J1 (4-pin header in), U1 (ESDA6V1BC6, a four-channel TVS array: the KiCad library's own symbol and SOT-23-6 footprint), J2 (4-pin header out). Both headers carry D+, GND, D-, VBUS on pins 1-4; each data line flows through U1, D+ in on pin 1 and out on pin 6, D- on 3 and 4, a TVS channel to ground at each, and both COM pins (2 and 5), which the part joins inside, are on GND. Tracks 0.25 mm on KiCad's default rules. It passes kicad-cli pcb drc at every severity with nothing unconnected, carries the library's pin names on every pad, and runs VBUS and GND at 0.5 A. Its schematic, esd_guard.kicad_sch, is the same circuit on KiCad's stock symbols, every footprint on the board linked to its symbol: it passes kicad-cli sch erc at every severity and matches the board exactly. The project's own sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table name the stock libraries, so ERC reads the same on a host whose KiCad was never configured. selftest/assets/make_baseline.py made all of it, and says how. vbus_droop.cir models the VBUS path from the host through the cable and the board to J2 under a 0.5 A step, and dips to 4.83 V against USB 2.0's 4.75 V. esd_guard.kicad_dru holds one custom rule (usb_pair: the data pair at least 0.2 mm wide), which the 0.25 mm tracks keep and pcb.drc's probes show live; esd_guard.symbols.json is the statement pcb.schematic_from_board writes the same circuit from. esda6v1bc6_land.json is ST's recommended SOT23-6L land, numbered by function, which KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits to 0.0125 mm. power_board.kicad_pcb (make_power_board.py) is a second board, placed and netted but not routed, that only the four battery rules read: a USB-C receptacle in, an MCP73833-AMI/UN charger with its THERM on an NTC and PROG on 3k, a PTC between the cell's connector BT1 and VSYS, a one-cell protector sensing the cell through the PTC and 330 ohm and driving a dual N-MOSFET in the cell's negative lead, a wire out, and two 8-position FFC housings. enclosure.step is a closed 2 mm box around the populated board, its lid 2.365 mm over the header pins; the footprints' 3D models are KiCad's own, kept in selftest/assets/3d/ so the fit sees the same parts on every host.

main.source: a one-cell pack on an LG INR18650 MJ1 cell, its protection board in the pack and a two-wire pigtail to BT1. LG Chem product specification LRB-PS-CY3500_MJ1, rev 1, 2016-06-30, read 2026-11-24: 2.4 max charge voltage 4.2 +- 0.05 V (upper_charge_v 4.25), 2.5 max charge current 1.0 C, 3350 mA, 2.6 end voltage (cut off) 2.5 V, 2.9 charge 0 ~ 45 C. short_a is a fixture estimate, not measured: the cell (4.2.1: at most 40 mOhm initial AC impedance), the pack's FETs and the pigtail in series, 10 A at the least and 40 A at the most

charger.source: Microchip MCP73833/4 datasheet DS22005B (2009), read 2026-11-24: THERM is pin 8 of the MSOP-10 (KiCad's MCP73833-xxx-UN symbol); VREG 4.168-4.232 V for the 4.20 V option; IREG = 1000 V / RPROG, 900-1100 mA at PROG 1.0 kOhm (k_v 900-1100 V); ITHERM 47-53 uA, VT1 1.20-1.26 V, VT2 0.235-0.265 V; the AMI option is 4.20 V with its timer disabled (0 hours). R3 is 1 %. TH1 is a fixture NTC, 10 kOhm +- 1 %, B25/85 4250 K +- 1 %, not a product's

protector.source: fixture values, not a product's: a one-cell protector on KiCad's AP9101CK symbol pins (VM 1, VDD 2, VSS 3, DO 4, CO 5), overcharge detection 4.35 V at the most, overdischarge detection 2.85 V at the least; VDD through F1 and R5 (330 ohm) from the cell; DO and CO on the gates of Q1 (KiCad's FDS6890A symbol: S1 1, G1 2, S2 3, G2 4), whose sources sit on the cell's negative and on ground

pack_pcm.source: fixture values, not a product's: the pack's own protection board, overcharge 4.30 V at the most, overdischarge 2.30 V at the least, as a pack drawing would state them

fuse.source: fixture values, not a product's: a PTC that holds 0.5 A, trips by 1.0 A, trips within 0.1 s at 8 A, and breaks 80 A

wire_out.source: 26 AWG solid copper, 0.405 mm across, 0.129 mm^2 (ASTM B258), PVC insulated: 70 C in service and 160 C its short-circuit limit (IEC 60364-5-54's k = 115 pair); continuous_a 1.0 A is a fixture rating, not a standard's

flex.source: fixture: an 8-way FFC from J10 to J11, contacts on the same side at both ends, so position n meets position n

_notes._units: Millimetres for every length (KiCad's file unit), amperes, degrees C of rise above ambient, ounces of copper per square foot (1 oz = 35 um = 1.378 mil).
_notes._paths: pcb_board, pcb_spice_deck and pcb_enclosure_step resolve against the PROJECT ROOT (ctx.root). Its project file (.kicad_pro), custom rules (.kicad_dru) and schematic (.kicad_sch, with every sheet under it) when they exist beside it with the same name, and the project's sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table, go with it to kicad-cli: they hold the design rules, KiCad's ERC and DRC exclusions and the libraries.
_notes.pcb_board: The board this pack checks. One board per project projection; a project with two boards scopes the key (pcb.pcb_board) per model, or runs two projects.
_notes.pcb_net_currents_a: {net: amperes} for every net whose current matters. pcb.net_width judges only the nets named here, because the board does not say what flows where. 0.5 A on VBUS and GND is a USB 2.0 port's budget.
_notes.pcb_temp_rise_limit_c: How far above ambient a track may run, degrees C. 10 C is the common design choice and the bottom of IPC-2221's fitted range (10-100 C): below it the formula is extrapolation, and the verdict says so.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_outer: Copper weight of the outer layers. 1 oz is what a fab quotes without being asked; the gate uses that and says '[pack default]' when this key is absent.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_inner: Copper weight of inner layers, 0.5 oz by the same convention. Unused on this two-layer board.
_notes.pcb_drc_severity: all (the default), error or warning. 'all' because a check at error severity cannot see a warning, and the fab still prints the silk a warning is about. Waive a finding by excluding it in KiCad, which records it in the .kicad_pro: never by narrowing this.
_notes.pcb_drc_timeout_s: Wall clock for one kicad-cli run. This board takes well under a second, a 4-layer board of about a hundred footprints about 2 s; 120 s is for a hang, which reads as a skip.
_notes.pcb_erc_severity: all (the default), error or warning, for pcb.erc, by the same reasoning as pcb_drc_severity. The schematic is the board's name with .kicad_sch (KiCad's rule for a project's root schematic) unless pcb_schematic names another for ERC; pcb.parity always compares with the board's own, as KiCad does.
_notes.pcb_fab: The fab whose published limits pcb.fab_rules holds the board to: jlcpcb (gates/fab/jlcpcb.json, each number quoted from its capability page with the day it was read), or a path from the project root to a fab file of the same shape. The row is chosen, in the service pcb_fab_service names, by the board's copper layer count and pcb_copper_oz_outer.
_notes.pcb_fab_service: Which of the fab file's services the board is ordered on: each service lists the dielectrics and via kinds it builds, and a board whose stackup names another dielectric, or that holds another via kind, skips rather than be judged on that service's rows. It may be left out when the file has one service; with several and none named, the gate skips, naming them. standard is JLCPCB's FR-4 service with through vias; this board states no stackup, so it is KiCad's default FR4.
_notes.pcb_spice_deck: The SPICE deck pcb.spice runs with ngspice -b, from the project root. The deck is the project's model of the circuit, not the board: ngspice solves what it says. Relative .include and .lib paths resolve from the deck's directory.
_notes.pcb_spice_measure: The .meas result the verdict reads (ngspice lowercases names; so does the gate).
_notes.pcb_spice_min: The lowest value that passes, in pcb_spice_units. 4.75 V is USB 2.0's minimum VBUS at a high-power port's device connector. pcb_spice_max is the highest; give either or both.
_notes.pcb_spice_units: The measure's units, as ngspice computes it (SI: V, A, s). Stated by the project, because the gate cannot tell which quantity a .meas measures.
_notes.pcb_spice_timeout_s: Wall clock for one ngspice run. The baseline deck solves in about 0.01 s.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_step: The enclosure's solid (its walls and lid, the material, not the cavity) as a STEP file in mm, from the project root. The baseline's is a closed box made by selftest/assets/make_enclosure.py around the populated baseline board.
_notes.pcb_board_placement: Where the board sits in the enclosure's frame: turned rot_z_deg about z, then moved by x, y, z mm. The board's own frame is kicad-cli's STEP export with --user-origin 0x0mm: the board file's (0, 0) at the origin, x right, y up (KiCad's y negated), z up from the board's bottom face.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_clearance_mm: The smallest gap any part may keep from the enclosure. 1 mm is a common allowance for print and assembly tolerance; the board body itself may touch (it sits on standoffs). The baseline's nearest part, a header, is 2.365 mm under the lid.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_bodiless: References of placed parts that have no body to fit (an antenna drawn in copper): each listed is a statement that the fit need not see it. Every other SMD or through-hole part must name a 3D model that kicad-cli finds, or pcb.enclosure_fit skips.
_notes.pcb_fit_timeout_s: Wall clock for the STEP export and for the geometry, each. The baseline takes about 1 s and 3 s.
_notes.pcb_pin_names_ignore: Pin names pcb.pin_names never compares: unused-pin names, which may sit on any net, and KiCad's hidden-name placeholder. Every other repeated name must carry one net.
_notes.pcb_pin_names_series: {ref: {pairs: [[pin, pin]], source}}: on that ref, each pair is the two ends of one series element that the library names alike (an EMI filter array names both ends of a channel CH1), so it may carry two nets. A pair must name the only two pins of the ref that carry its name, or the gate errors: the record is for another design. A pair stated on one ref clears nothing on another. Empty here: the ESD array's two COM pins are one node inside the part, not a series pair.
_notes.pcb_land_drawings: {ref: drawing record} for pcb.land_pattern, each a JSON file from the project root: {part, source, view: "top", y_axis: "up" (as printed) or "down" (as a KiCad footprint), pads: [{number, function, x, y, w, h}]} in mm. The baseline holds U1 to ST's recommended SOT23-6L land; KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits it to 0.0125 mm.
_notes.pcb_batteries: {id: record}, one per battery (an object keyed by id, not a list: the mutation walk reaches an object's leaves, and other records point at the ids). Each: board (else pcb_board); terminals {ref, value, pos, neg, therm (the pack's thermistor pin, or null), taps (for two or more cells in series, the junction pins from the lowest up)}; chemistry (li-ion, li-polymer, lifepo4, lto, nimh, li-primary or alkaline: it picks which rules apply, never a number); series and parallel (whole numbers); cell, each value per cell from the cell's datasheet: upper_charge_v (the upper limit charging voltage, with its tolerance), discharge_v_min, charge_a_max, charge_temp_c [lo, hi] (the widest window any charge is allowed in) and short_a [least, most] or internal_resistance_ohm [least, most]; ntc (the pack's NTC: r25_ohm, r25_tol_pct, beta_tol_pct (with a table too: state 0 only for an exact table), and rt_table_c_ohm [[C, ohm], ...] or beta_k and beta_pair_c); source. A rule that needs a value the record lacks errors, naming it. The baseline's records name power_board.kicad_pcb, a board only these four tier-0 rules read.
_notes.pcb_protectors: {id: record}, one per protecting element, holding every function it serves. Each: battery (an id in pcb_batteries); kind (charger, protector, pack-pcm, bms, gauge, fuse, ptc, efuse or blocking: a charger stops its own charge, every other kind says how it acts); where (board, in-pack or firmware: an in-pack element counts on its datasheet's word, firmware is named and never counted); board, ref and value when on the board; functions, any of: charge_v {v_reg_v [min, max] or divider {vfb_v, top_ref, bottom_ref, tol_pct}, per_cell, set_by}, charge_a {a_max, or prog {ref, k_v [min, max], r_tol_pct}, set_by}, charge_temp {sense {pin, kind current with i_a, cold_v, hot_v, or kind ratio with pullup_ref, pullup_tol_pct, cold_frac, hot_frac}, ntc {ref, value, r25_ohm, r25_tol_pct, beta_tol_pct, and rt_table_c_ohm or beta_k and beta_pair_c} or {battery_therm: true}, network {series_ref, parallel_ref, tol_pct, others}, acts {pin, to {ref, pin}}; in the pack: window_c {cold_c, hot_c}}, overcharge_v {v_max, per_cell, sense, acts}, overdischarge_v {v_min, per_cell, sense {pin, through [refs]} or {taps}, acts {pin, switch {ref, value, control, path}}}, trip {kind fuse, ptc, fet, efuse or pcm, terminal pos or neg, path_pins or switch, hold_a, trip_a, trip_max_s [[A, s]], interrupt_a, ahead [{ref, value, why}]}, safety_timer (evidence only); source. A field shown as [min, max] (and i_a, cold_v, hot_v, cold_frac, hot_frac, vfb_v, window_c's cold_c and hot_c) is the datasheet range and refuses one number. A field that takes one number takes the datasheet's guaranteed bound on the side that protects less, never its typical, and the rule cannot tell the two apart: v_max is the most overcharge detection voltage, v_min the least overdischarge detection voltage, a_max the most charge current, trip_a the current by which the part is sure to trip, trip_max_s the longest time at each current, interrupt_a the current it is rated to break.
_notes.pcb_conductors: {id: record}, each a conductor a cell can drive a fault through: battery; board; kind (wire, ffc, contact or track); for a track, net and continuous_rise_c (its rating is IPC-2221 at that rise, on its narrowest stretch); otherwise ref, value, pins (all on one net), area_mm2 of ONE conductor (parallel contacts get no credit) and continuous_a; start_c (its temperature in service) and limit_c (what its insulation allows in a fault); protected_by (the protector ids that guard it); source. pcb.fault_current turns on limit_c and continuous_a: say where each comes from.
_notes.pcb_matings: {id: record}, each a connector that meets another: a and b, each {board, ref, value}; map (straight, reversed, or {a_pin: b_pin}); source. The power rules join the two pads' nets, so an element on another board counts.
